paragraphs: The M135i has been the performance flagship of the BMW 1 Series range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. The original F20/F21-generation car (2012 to 2019) uses the N55 — a 3.0-litre straight-six turbo petrol shared with the 3 Series and 4 Series of that era, and widely regarded as a strong, well-proven engine. From 2019, the F40-generation M135i switched to the B48 — a 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo petrol, a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the N55. The B48 is the same engine family used across BMW's modern range and is generally considered reliable. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ — which is why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting. The F20/F21 M135i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre straight-six turbo petrol fitted to the M135i from 2012 to 2019 (F20/F21 generation). Well-regarded overall with minimal major issues documented in specialist circles. We service this engine to the same standard as our other M135i rebuilds.

The current 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo petrol, fitted to the M135i from 2019 onwards (F40 generation). This is part of BMW's newer modular engine family and is generally considered more reliable than earlier BMW turbo fours.

compatibility.intro: Because the M135i spans two distinct engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N55 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N55 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M135i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
